speaker: (the stationer)
text: Master Shakespeare. He is within, and the wardens are on the table. I asked you to an ordinary to meet my poet, and I have a shutter to put up.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: You are good to come. I am not always good at a noise. Sit, if the bench will bear two men who would rather have a book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The bench will bear us. I bought your Civil Wars in April, at a stall, for two shillings. I had stood and read it longer than the two shillings deserved. The stanzas taught me where to look.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: Then I owe the stall a kindness, and you nothing. I came to Shoreditch last week, in a plain cloak, to see the king played. I still mistrust a penny yard.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny yard is a loud school. What did it do to the cloak?

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: It put a boy in a garden, speaking the Queen's sorrow aloud. My own stanzas on that same queen have seemed cold marble beside it ever since. I have been reading them over. I do not like them so well.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Cold marble is a hard judge of a page. The boy is the warmer instrument. I am not sure he is the truer one.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: History is a stern master. You have been kinder to Richard than I was, and less kind to the truth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Where your chronicle bends, I have sometimes gone straight, and where I cheat, your stanza keeps its foot on the date. Which is the better lie is a question for two craftsmen, and not for a quarrel.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: I hear you put a gardener in. I should not have dared.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The gardener is a way of saying in public what a chronicle says in a margin. I do not think I won by it. I think I was heard.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: Eat. The wardens are baked, and the claret is a cup, not a reputation. I saw you set the crust aside.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The jaw manages the wardens and declines the crust. It is mended enough for fruit. It is not in a humour for a boast.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: Then the crust can go to the house. I will not make a point of a man's mouth. We were speaking of a joint in a piece of work, and a joint is fitter than a victory.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Fitter. I am more pleased than a supper warrants, and I do not mean to turn the pleasure into a story for strangers.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: Nor I. Paul's Chain is the way I go. If you go by Cheapside, we can part at the Chain as two men who have not scored a hit.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At the Chain, then. No edge. I am glad Waterson asked, and gladder he knew when to leave.

speaker: samuel_daniel
text: He knows his shutters. Good night, Master Shakespeare. The marble will have to bear the comparison. I will not ask the boy to be duller so that my page can feel safe.
